_description: CAREER arm B: ontology-guided NEGATIVE SELECTION only, single factor. Identical to config/lc_career_baseline.json except ontology_guided_negatives=true. Sample-level ontology weighting stays OFF (ontology_weight=0.0) and optimal transport stays OFF, so the contrast against the baseline isolates one mechanism.
_why_single_factor: The existing results_v7_lc_*_ontology runs changed FOUR things at once versus vanilla: ontology_weight 0.0->0.3 (sample-level loss weighting), use_pathway_negatives False->True and pathway_weight 0.0->0.8 (negative selection), and use_ot_distance False->True (an extra ontology signal). Their +0.0226 at 10% therefore cannot be attributed to any one mechanism, and the non-monotonic curve plus the ISCO arm going negative at 50% are consistent with the components pulling in different directions. ontology_guided_negatives exists specifically to decouple selection from weighting: it builds the skill matcher regardless of ontology_weight.
_paired_with: config/lc_trials_ontneg_only.json — the same single mechanism (ontology-tiered negative selection) implemented over MeSH instead of ESCO, so the two datasets can share one table.
_comment_cache: Same dedicated path as the baseline arm, deliberately. Text embeddings come from the FROZEN encoder, so they are arm-independent and sharing them makes the second arm's runs fast without leaking anything learned between arms.
_comment_the_factor: THE ONE THING THAT VARIES. ontology_guided_negatives=true builds the ESCO skill matcher and routes negative selection through _select_ontology_negatives, which tiers candidates by skill-graph distance. ontology_negative_rank_tiers=true is required, not optional: the absolute cut points (d<=0.3 hard) are never reached on career v7, where the hardest job for a resume sits near d~0.5, so with absolute tiering the hard bucket is always empty and ontology injects no hard negatives at all.
_comment_held_off: Everything else ontology-related is OFF so the contrast is single-factor.
_comment_skill_distances: Seeds the matcher's distance cache. The previously hardcoded skill_distances.pkl (116,848 pairs) covers only 0.6% of the skill pairs formed by the 5,292 distinct ESCO URIs in this dataset, so ~99% of lookups became nx.shortest_path_length calls on the full ESCO KG and a single 640-record epoch stalled for many minutes. The v7 pickle (11,675,625 pairs) covers 68.9% of the same sample. Distances are identical either way — this is purely cost. Set in BOTH arms so it cannot become a second factor; it is inert in the baseline, which builds no matcher.
_comment_seed: Must be set per run. The existing learning-curve runs have training_seed=null, which is why their single-run deltas cannot be separated from the +/-0.013 seed spread measured on the 5-seed full-data comparison.
